    vitti a = ganita_vargmool(n)
    vitti b = 1
    vitti k = a * a - n
    # Perfect squares (k == 0) have only the trivial (1, 0)
    # solution; the search would divide by |k| = 0.
    yadi (k == 0) {
        out[0] = 1
        out[1] = 0
        nivartanam 1
    }
    vitti guard = 0
    yavat (k != 1) {
        # Pick m with (a + b*m) divisible by |k| minimising
        # |m*m - n|. The old m = 0, 1, 2, ... scan hangs
        # for large |k|; solve b*m = -a (shesh |k|) with
        # kuttaka, then compare the two candidates
        # bracketing sqrt(n) (f is convex in m).
        vitti ak = ganita_nirapeksh(k)
        vitti g1 = b
        vitti g2 = ak
        yavat (g2 != 0) {
            vitti gt = g1 % g2
            g1 = g2
            g2 = gt
        }
        yadi (a % g1 != 0) { nivartanam 0 }
        vitti m0 = kuttaka(b, ak, 0 - a)
        vitti varg = ganita_vargmool(n)
        vitti d = varg - m0
        vitti t = d / ak
        vitti r = d % ak
        yadi (d < 0 && r != 0) { t = t - 1 }
        vitti bf = 0 - 1
        vitti bm = 0
        vitti bn = 0
        vitti cnt = 0
        yavat (cnt < 2) {
            vitti m = m0 + t * ak
            yadi (m >= 0 && m <= 3037000499) {
                # num = m*m - n, exact. m > isqrt(MAX)
                # candidates are skipped; the below one
                # is always exact, so one remains.
                vitti ank = m * m - n
                vitti f = ank
                yadi (f < 0) { f = 0 - f }
                yadi (bf < 0 || f < bf) {
                    bf = f
                    bm = m
                    bn = ank
                }
            }
            t = t + 1
            cnt = cnt + 1
        }
        yadi (bf < 0) { nivartanam 0 }
        vitti mm = bm
        # Overflow in na/nb/nk returns 0, not a wrap.
        yadi (a != 0 && mm > 9223372036854775807 / a) { nivartanam 0 }
        vitti amm = a * mm
        yadi (b != 0 && n > 9223372036854775807 / b) { nivartanam 0 }
        vitti nbp = n * b

# --- checked / saturating integer arithmetic (R18) ---
#
# MECHANISM (decided, with reasoning): these functions are OPT-IN.
# The plain `+ - * / %` operators are UNCHANGED and still wrap
# silently — changing them needs a compiler change (see the follow-on
# proposal at the end of this section), and silently changing every
# program's arithmetic would rewrite accepted behaviour. Instead,
# code that must not be wrong calls a checked function and reads
# ok[0] (the varna_tak_ank ok-pattern: ok is a 1-cell mala). On
# failure the function returns 0 — never the wrapped value — so a
# caller that forgets to check ok gets an obviously-wrong 0, not a
# plausible-but-wrong wrapped value.
#
# What the operators do today (measured, R18, current compiler):
#   + - * overflow  -> silent two's-complement wrap
#   / % by zero     -> hardware SIGFPE: the process DIES (exit 136),
#                      with no diagnostic naming the operation
#   INT64_MIN / -1  -> same SIGFPE (idiv overflow)
#   INT64_MIN % -1  -> same SIGFPE
#   INT64_MIN * -1  -> silent wrap to INT64_MIN
# So division is already "loud" in the sense that the process dies,
# but undiagnosed and unrecoverable. The checked functions give the
# diagnosed, recoverable path: ok[0] = 0 and the program continues.
#
# FOLLOW-ON (needs src/ changes, NOT done here): a compiler trap —
# emit a conditional check after each arithmetic op (jo/jno on the
# overflow flag for + - *, a zero-divisor guard before idiv) that
# aborts with a diagnostic naming file:line and the operation. The
# checked functions here are the library-level half of that work
# and would stay as the explicit form even after a trap exists.
#
# Bounds used below: MAX = 9223372036854775807, MIN is written as
# (0 - 9223372036854775807) - 1 (no MIN literal exists).

prakriya khand_yuj(parts, count, sep, sepn, out) {
    vitti p = parts
    vitti cnt = count
    vitti sp = sep
    vitti splen = sepn
    vitti dst = out
    vitti rpos = 0
    vitti wpos = 0
    vitti si = 0
    vitti seglen = 0
    vitti k = 0
    vitti q = 0
    yavat (si < cnt) {
        seglen = p[rpos]
        rpos = rpos + 1
        # pack writes a 0 byte at dst[wpos+seglen]; the separator (or
        # the final terminator below) overwrites it.
        # Cell index -> byte offset: rpos * 8.
        khand_bandh(p + rpos * 8, seglen, dst + wpos)
        wpos = wpos + seglen
        rpos = rpos + seglen
        yadi (si < cnt - 1) {
            q = 0
            yavat (q < splen) {
                akshar_rakh(dst, wpos, akshar(sp, q))
                wpos = wpos + 1
                q = q + 1
            }
        }
        si = si + 1
    }
    akshar_rakh(dst, wpos, 0)
    nivartanam wpos
}

prakriya khand_viparyay(src, sn, out) {
    vitti s = src
    vitti n = sn
    vitti dst = out
    vitti i = 0
    vitti j = 0
    vitti t = 0
    yadi (n <= 0) {
        akshar_rakh(dst, 0, 0)
        nivartanam 0
    }
    i = 0
    j = n - 1
    yavat (i < j) {
        t = akshar(s, i)
        akshar_rakh(dst, i, akshar(s, j))
        akshar_rakh(dst, j, t)
        i = i + 1
        j = j - 1
    }
    yadi (n % 2 == 1) {
        akshar_rakh(dst, n / 2, akshar(s, n / 2))
    }
    akshar_rakh(dst, n, 0)
    nivartanam n
}

prakriya madhava_cos(dasham x) {
    dasham pi2 = 6.283185307179586
    dasham pi = 3.141592653589793
    vitti k = x / pi2
    dasham y = x - k * pi2
    yadi (y > pi) { y = y - pi2 }
    yadi (y < 0.0 - pi) { y = y + pi2 }
    dasham s = 1.0
    dasham t = 1.0
    vitti n = 1
    yavat (n < 16) {
        t = 0.0 - t * y * y / ((2.0 * n - 1.0) * (2.0 * n))
        s = s + t
        n = n + 1
    }
    nivartanam s
}
